messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: Elevated 5xx rates from private VPC customers egressing through our peering gateway -> multiple 502/504 + timeouts. Alert group: inference-gateway-egress-high-5xx. See runbook link: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/egress-5xx

ashley: oncall here, acknowledged. seeing the alert graphs — spike started ~1923456700. Which customers impacted?

priya: I can confirm 3 private customers showing >15% 5xx for last 3 min on the gateway route. Also seeing connection resets. Pulling logs now.

matt: quick check: gateway pods healthy, cpu low, but upstream responses are 502. nginx proxy shows upstream reset-by-peer frequently.

priya: running a curl from one of the affected VPCs:
```
$ curl -v https://inference-gw.internal/health
* Connected to inference-gw.internal (10.10.5.7) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference-gw.internal
> 
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< 
* Connection #0 to host inference-gw.internal left intact
```

ashley: that matches. Are we seeing NAT ephemeral port saturation? recent incidents looked similar.

sre-bot: Automated check: NATGateway SNAT port utilization > 92% on nat-01 in us-west-2 for private-peering-vpc. Conntrack count high on transit appliance: 487k (threshold 400k). Route table flaps observed at 1923456725 and 1923456740.

matt: route flaps + high conntrack can cause asymmetric flows -> upstream timeouts + 502s. Any recent infra change?

jordan: networking team: we rolled a peering re-route 3m ago to drain a transit appliance (controlled rollout). I see one security-group update at 1923456698 that tightened egress rules for a helper service — could be unrelated.

priya: looking at netstat on transit appliance (snippet):
```
tcp  0 0 10.10.5.7:443  10.20.8.33:54712  ESTABLISHED
... many TIME_WAIT/TCP_RETRANS entries ...
```

ashley: customer impact: several inference requests failing for private VPC customers using peering + NAT egress. Marking Sev2, notify CS.

cs-team: we have two live customer chats, escalating to CS leads. Preparing templated message for status page.

ops-oncall: proposed immediate mitigations:
- stop the peering re-route (rollback) to stabilize pathing
- increase NAT capacity (launch additional NAT or swap to larger NAT)
- temporarily relax SG egress to allow ephemeral port ranges (if safe)
- apply rate limiting on the gateway to slow traffic surge
Which one should we do first?

matt: first -> rollback the route change to restore symmetric pathing. Second -> spin up extra NATs to relieve SNAT pressure. Third -> if still high, broaden SG egress to ephemeral ports.

jordan: rolling back route now (executing):
```
> aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 10.0.0.0/8 --gateway-id tgw-01-old
```

sre-bot: Route rollback acknowledged at 1923456795. Metrics: RTT on peering path dropping, retransmits decreasing. Conntrack dropping from 487k -> 360k after ~20s.

priya: launching additional NAT instance pool (autoscale group). Command:
```
> aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-nat --count 2 --instance-type t3.large --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=nattmp}]'
```

ops-oncall: NAT instances provisioned and registered to route tables at 1923456820. SNAT utilization dropping to 55%. 5xx rate falling from 18% -> 4% across impacted customers.

ashley: good. CS: send initial customer update noting partial mitigation and ongoing monitoring. Status page: "Degraded — some private VPC customers may experience 5xx/timeouts when using peering egress. We're mitigating by restoring route and increasing NAT capacity."

cs-team: sent to customers and posted status. Two customers requested ETA, we gave 30m estimate and offered workarounds: shift to Hosted API or use dedicated egress.

matt: follow-up action items while we keep monitoring:
- networking to audit the SG change that tightened egress for helper service (jordan)
- infra to implement autoscaling for NAT pool to prevent future depletion (priya)
- consider adding conntrack alarms on transit appliances (ashley)
- write postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps (ops-oncall)

jordan: SG rule that tightened egress was applied by infra-automation @ 1923456698. Rolling that revert and we'll add tests to prevent overly broad tightening on peering subnets.

priya: leaving a watch on metrics for next 45m. If 5xx <1% and no further flaps, we'll move to mitigated status.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigation in progress. Next update due 20m.

ashley: handing off to night oncall (mira) at 1923456860 — Mira, brief: route rollback + extra NATs in place, conntrack recovered, 5xx down to 3-4%. Watch SNAT ports and route stability. If 5xx rises above 8% re-page SRE.

ops-oncall: Handoff ack. I'll capture incident id INC-2026-345 and start the postmortem doc.

cs-team: final note: customers asked for root cause summary and compensation options. Creating a CS ticket to coordinate comms after postmortem.
